context: PR preview workflow. A teammate wired it up to actually build and deploy the PR's code so reviewers can click a live link.
explanation: This combines two dangerous things: `pull_request_target` runs with the base repo's secrets and a token with write access, and the new `ref:` on checkout pulls in the PR head — i.e. the fork author's own code. The workflow then runs `npm ci`/`npm run build` (executing that untrusted code) and hands it a real deploy token via env. Any external contributor can open a PR that exfiltrates `PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN` or does anything else the token can do. Fix: either stay on `pull_request` (no secrets, no elevated token) or, if `pull_request_target` is required, never check out the PR head and never build/execute PR-controlled code in that context.
